pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Thallium Toxicity (Thallium Poisoning) THE SMOKING GUN: Rapid onset of diffuse hair loss (alopecia) paired with severe, painful peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy (allodynia) and autonomic instability following initial gastrointestinal distress. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Thallium chemically mimics potassium due to its nearly identical ionic radius. It replaces potassium in the Na+/K+-ATPase pump and interferes with cellular respiration by inhibiting vital enzymes such as pyruvate kinase and succinate dehydrogenase. Tissues with high energy demands and high cell turnover, specifically peripheral nerve axons, keratinocytes, and hair follicle matrix cells, experience severe mitochondrial disruption and intracellular energy failure, resulting in acute axonal neuropathy and total hair shedding.
